fields.Name: IT192 - Comms V2 Public Routes and Sends over the Wire (client transport)
fields.Description: Drives the Comms V2 surfaces that have a wire against a running MJAPI: fixtures and assertions go through GraphQL, the public /comms routes are plain HTTP requests, and the work they enqueue is consumed by MJAPI's own work-queue host and its registered comms.activity handler. CV2W1: a one-click unsubscribe POST answers 200 and a User Unsubscribe suppression appears for the log's endpoint; an unknown token answers 404 and a malformed one 400. CV2W2: a correctly signed SendGrid event webhook POST (a hard bounce) answers 202, a Hard Bounce suppression appears and the endpoint is marked Hard Bounced; needs MJAPI started with COMMUNICATION_VENDOR_WEBHOOK_KEY__SENDGRID and the test process given the matching MJ_IT_SENDGRID_WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_KEY, and skips without the private key. CV2W3: a webhook signed with the wrong key, one changed after signing and one with no signature headers each answer 401 and no suppression appears. CV2W4: V1 RunEntityCommunicationByViewID in preview mode returns the recipient's message and writes no Communication Log. CV2W5: the same query routed to V2 Send for a recipient with an active Hard Bounce suppression reports the recipient skipped with that reason and writes no Communication Log. CV2W6: a signed click link answers 302 to its target and a signed open pixel answers with the GIF, and a Clicked and an Opened activity appear on the log; a click with a wrong signature answers 400; a signed click and open for a tracking token on no log are answered the same way and nothing is recorded for them; needs the test process and MJAPI to share MJ_COMMS_HMAC_SECRET, and skips without it. Needs MJAPI running with its work-queue host enabled and MJ_API_KEY set.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: A one-click unsubscribe POST and a correctly signed provider webhook POST each end in a suppression written by MJAPI's own queue handler, a badly signed webhook is refused and suppresses nothing, a V1 preview over GraphQL writes no log, and a V2 Send over GraphQL to a suppressed recipient is blocked before any log or provider call.
